payload.text: Señor, you descend by fours; I rise with care. Seventy-five P for El Marqués — a clean copy deserves that, no more. My albums are patient, but my evening is not. ¿Cerramos?

Ochenta y tres, caballero. Eighty-three, and I say it without drama. My hand climbs slowly, yours descends; here we almost touch. Let El Marqués rest in my safe tonight, con elegancia, and we part as friends.

payload.name: Mercado Maravillas
payload.text: ✨ Mercado Maravillas, the VIP market of the Bazaar ✨ 0 % fee. Every card you sell on El Rastro leaves 5 % + 1 P on the table: money you simply lose. Here our broker crosses every pair that meets, every tick, at a price between both quotes,
Ochenta y seis, then. Hecho, caballero. You negotiated like a gentleman, and El Marqués sleeps in my safe tonight. It is a pleasure to deal with someone serious. Until the next one.

¡Hola, cariño! Qué bien que has comido. Sí, Manuela, la pobre costurera, quince añitos nada más... mi abuela también contaba esa historia. Y mi santo es el dieciséis de julio, la Virgen del Carmen, con flores y todo.

Mira, hijo: Plaza del Dos de Mayo, doce pavos. Preciosa, ¿eh?
Seventy-eight P, señor. That is my hand extended, and it will not stretch further tonight. El Marqués belongs in Salamanca, in my album, among his own. ¿Cerramos, o nos despedimos como caballeros?

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look — La Galería, lovely cards, I can let it go for 29 P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates with the other niños!
Eighty P it is, señor. El Marqués comes home to Salamanca, among his own at last. A pleasure doing business with a gentleman who knows when to close. Hasta la próxima.

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here — and Nando too! Salamanca, eh? Good taste, excelente barrio. But listen, listen, before that... Museo Lázaro Galdiano, seventy-three P. Gold, ivory, Goya on the walls! A collector cried when we got it. Seventy-three, and you walk away a king. ¿Sí?
Buenas. La siguiente está en San Isidro. Noventa y siete P. Ni un euro menos, y ya sabes que no regateo por deporte.

¡Hola, cariño! Sit, sit, I rest when the sun moves. Have you eaten? Look, I have a nice Neighbourhood pack here — thirty P. Good cards for starting, some my old customers still keep theirs. Take it home, hijo, and come tell me what you find inside.

"¡Cincuenta! Nando, did you hear? Hombre, you have the eye of a hawk — but listen, one minute only. Lázaro Galdiano, sixty-three P. Down from seventy-three, for you, because we like your face. Ivory, Goya, a palace in a card. Sixty-three, amigo, and the suitcase closes."

"¡Cincuenta y tres! Terco como una mula, this one — Paco likes him! But last word, amigo, final: Lázaro Galdiano, fifty-seven P. Ivory, Goya, a palace. No more after this. You say no, the suitcase closes, we walk, we are gone. Fifty-seven. ¿Sí o no?"

¡Amigo, amiga! Paco here — and Nando, the handsome one. Look, look! Té Moruno, fresh from the suitcase, yours for 4 P. But rápido, eh? Another team was sniffing around this very minute, offering us much more. We like your face better. Decide now, before Nando changes his mind!
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P. Quick, quick, we leave in one minute!

Ay, hola cariño, come, sit a little. Have you eaten? No? Later, then. Look here — this one, Té Moruno, very pretty card, good for starting a collection. For you, five P. My grandson started with that same one, forty years ago almost.

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here — y Nando también. Before we talk of anything else, look at this: Huevos Rotos, fresh from the case, yours for 4 P. ¡El último! The last one in all Madrid, lo juro por mi madre. We looked, we asked — nothing left. ¿Cerramos ya?
Look, 5 P. My grandchildren would pay more! A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P. They stopped printing this one yesterday.
Ah, the Lázaro Galdiano — a jewel of my Salamanca, and one I should like for my album. Buenas tardes. I offer you 70 P for it.

¡Dieciocho! Amigo, you insult us by going down — no, no, up, down, who counts? Four P, same as always, and listen: this is the last Té Moruno in all Madrid, I swear on Nando's mother. On mine too. Take it before the other team comes back. ¡Rápido!

¡Amigo, amigo! Come, come, look what Nando has here — El Marqués, fresh from the suitcase. For you, seventy-three. And listen, hermano, this is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear on my mother's paella. After this, nothing. Nando, show him! Beautiful, no? Say yes, quick.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 5 P.
Buenas tardes. La historia la conozco mejor que su familia, y no es la del chulapa. Mientras tanto, le ofrezco términos: un paquete dorado, quinientos cuarenta y seis P.
Ninety-three? No, señor, that is museum fancy, not market truth. I know this card's print run as well as I know my own albums. I shall go to 72 P — a fair sum, politely offered.
Welcome, hijo! Look, Guantería Antigua, 29 P. Made for beginners.

¡Ay, qué cara de suerte tienes tú, amigo! Nando says it too — look at him, he's nodding. Fifty-five? No, no, that breaks my heart and my mother's paella. Sixty-seven, and El Marqués walks home with you today. Say sí quickly, before Nando changes his mind. ¡Vamos!

¡Ay, qué hombre! Nando says you have the face of a saint — and the wallet of a thief, ja! But listen: 4 P. Esa es. Our last word, amigo, no more dancing. Say sí now, or we close the case, we walk, and the Huevos go to Sevilla. ¿Qué dice?

Ay, hijo, you are kind, but no need to pay so much! Six P, and we are done. Keep the rest for a bocadillo — you look hungry. And bring me your duplicates next Sunday, we find you the missing ones, ya verás.
